Draft (2–3 sentences for procurement doc):
Redwood processes requests on behalf of customers using our hosted API. We may route requests to subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, analytics) to provide the service; an up-to-date list of subprocessors and their locations is maintained here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRedwoodSubprocessorsList. Cross-border transfers are managed under our DPA and safeguarded with contractual and technical controls (TLS in transit, optional customer-managed keys).

Console snippet (single line for UI card):
"We process your API requests securely; see our current list of subprocessors and transfer safeguards."

Thanks Neha — nice draft. A few edits for procurement-friendly accuracy and a tighter console line. Quoting your draft below and adding inline suggestions.

> Redwood processes requests on behalf of customers using our hosted API.
Change to: "Redwood processes customer API requests in our hosted environment." (shorter / less passive)

> We may route requests to subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, analytics) to provide the service; an up-to-date list of subprocessors and their locations is maintained here: <drive link>.
Change to: "To deliver the service we rely on a small set of subprocessors (cloud infra, telemetry providers). An up-to-date list is published here: <drive link>."
Reason: procurement likes "published" and explicit examples.

> Cross-border transfers are managed under our DPA and safeguarded with contractual and technical controls (TLS in transit, optional customer-managed keys).
Small tweak: add "data residency options" as an on/off capability for customers who need it. Revised sentence: "Cross-border transfers are governed by our DPA and protected by contractual safeguards and technical measures (TLS in transit; optional customer-managed keys and residency controls)."

Console snippet suggestion (max 90 chars):
"Your API requests are protected — see subprocessors & transfer safeguards."

Other notes:
- Markus: can you confirm that "telemetry providers" is safe to mention publicly? If not, we'll replace with "operational providers."
- Vanessa: can you prep a one-line residency toggle copy if we want to surface that in the onboarding card?

If Acme needs a signed DPA, we should send Ben Stokes (copied by Alicia) our standard DPA and the certified subprocessor attestation; that usually satisfies procurement.

Laura Bennett
Director, Trust & Legal Enablement, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
